clue.text: The first with a drill when plane has corrosion in main body?

parts.note: a jet is a kind of aeroplane

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means its letters go inside the other word's letters

parts.note: the hull is the main body of a ship
rot is decay or corrosion

explanation.surface: A worker with a power drill notices an aircraft whose fuselage is badly corroded.
explanation.walkthrough: Jethro Tull was the 18th-century English farmer who invented the seed drill; the rock band took his name. 'Plane' looks like a carpenter's tool next to the drill.
explanation.definitionFit: The agriculturalist Jethro Tull devised the horse-drawn seed drill, the earliest machine of its kind for sowing crops in rows.

clue.text: Fair tournament? Nothing's been forgotten

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so a letter drops from the word

parts.note: a joust is a knightly tournament
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a competition was fair, since nothing seems to have been overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the O out of JOUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and fair are synonyms when describing impartial treatment or a decision based on right.

clue.text: Dainty material is cut

indicators.note: a word that is cut is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: tweed is a woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A delicate fabric is being snipped by a dressmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: TWEED loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for affectedly quaint or sweet, close to dainty in a cloying sense.

clue.text: The favourite for the nursery stakes?

definitions.text: The favourite for the nursery stakes?

parts.words: The favourite for the nursery stakes?
parts.note: surface reading: the horse tipped to win a race for young horses, a nursery stakes
setter's reading: the best-loved toy steed in a child's nursery

explanation.walkthrough: A nursery stakes is a real horse race for two-year-olds, so the clue sounds like racing tips; the horse is actually a toy in a child's room.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden toy horse on rockers is a classic plaything kept in a child's playroom, hence a nursery favourite.

clue.text: A little uprising — and in Latin country?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a bit is a little
et is Latin for and

explanation.surface: A small rebellion breaks out in a Latin-speaking land.
explanation.walkthrough: The uprising suggests a revolt, but it only turns BIT upside down. The 'and' is both link and fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a Himalayan region and historic nation, now administered by China.

clue.text: Nurse has air post

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance
post- as a prefix means after

explanation.surface: A hospital nurse has a job sending airmail.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to tend and care for them, which is the phrasal verb's meaning.

clue.text: Computer lingo's not about to make old Greek change

indicators.note: about is the Latin circa, and not having it removes that abbreviation

parts.note: COBOL is an early programming language
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Programming jargon fails to explain how to convert ancient Greek money.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C from COBOL. 'Change' here is coins, loose money.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, so it is old Greek small money.

clue.text: The problem comes up with a curate's organisation — he's officious

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: 'there's the rub' — the rub is the problem

indicators.note: organising things arranges them anew, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: letters of a curate rearranged

explanation.surface: A difficulty arises with the way a curate runs things, and he is a bossy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat is an official given to red tape, so a self-important, officious person fits.

clue.text: Unfasten the curtain — it's draped all over the sofa

definitions.text: it's draped all over the sofa

parts.note: to loose is to unfasten
a curtain is a cover

explanation.surface: Someone takes down a curtain and throws it over the settee.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cover is a removable fabric slip fitted over an armchair or settee, the British term for a slipcover.

clue.text: Play with reserve, making provision for a draw

definitions.note: a book is something provided for drawing in

parts.note: a sketch is a short comic play
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A drama played defensively ends in a stalemate result.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sporting draw; the draw is a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's pad of blank pages is supplied for making drawings, so it is a provision for drawing.

clue.text: Delivered second letter at last in Moravia

indicators.note: placed at last means put on the end of what remains

parts.note: a baby delivered is born
the second letter of the word for delivered

explanation.surface: A second letter arrived late in a central European region.
explanation.walkthrough: BORN with its second letter moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Brno is the chief city of Moravia, in the Czech Republic, so it is a city located in that region.

clue.text: Trains, moving smoothly in an invigorating way

indicators.note: something moving shifts about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters of trains rearranged
gently means smoothly

explanation.surface: Railway trains glide along in a refreshing manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent can mean bracing or sharply tonic, so the adverb describes acting in a stimulating, tightening manner.

clue.text: Interpret wrongly master's Latin?

indicators.note: things done wrongly are muddled, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: letters of master's Latin rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil makes a hash of rendering the schoolmaster's Latin text.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and the same words supply the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistranslate is to render a text incorrectly into another language, exactly getting a Latin passage wrong.

clue.text: Time my car's overhauled — it's not properly balanced

indicators.note: an overhauled engine is taken apart and rebuilt, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: letters of time my car's rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver books a car service because the vehicle pulls to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetric means lacking symmetry, with the two sides unequal, so it is lopsided.

clue.text: Came across a kind of check made on the board

definitions.text: a kind of check made on the board
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a chess check delivered when one piece moves and unmasks another

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled upon a special sort of inspection carried out by the directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The board looks like a company board; it is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Discovered means found; a discovered check in chess arises when moving one piece opens a line of attack for another.

clue.text: Informs about rookie's stolen weapon?

indicators.note: one word going about another wraps round it

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
L for learner, a novice
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A grass tells the police about a raw recruit's stolen gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult made of a forked stick and elastic is a child's missile launcher, a weapon only in a loose sense, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Plane making a curve — the result of hop and barley brew?

definitions.note: a noun phrase in effect: the curve a plane makes slicing a cone

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture stirred together, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: letters of hop and barley, without the and, rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft banks in an arc after a beer made with hops and barley.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is not an aircraft but a flat geometric plane: one cutting a double cone steeply produces this curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyperbola is a conic section, the open curve formed where a flat surface intersects both halves of a cone.

clue.text: Find the right page for the head of school right away

indicators.note: sent away means taken out of the word

parts.note: a rector heads some schools and colleges
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A headteacher urgently needs to locate the correct page.
explanation.walkthrough: RECTOR loses its final R. 'Head of school' wants to be a first letter, but here it is a whole title.
explanation.definitionFit: Recto is the printing term for the right-hand page of an open book.

clue.text: Still in supersonic aircraft, showing courage?

parts.note: speeds of supersonic aircraft are measured in Mach numbers
standing still is zero speed, nought

explanation.surface: A pilot calmly keeps his nerve while flying a supersonic jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Something standing still would register Mach nought, written MACH O.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes a showy, aggressive manliness, a display of toughness; the question mark admits it is bravado rather than real bravery.

clue.text: Issue a summons about a payment for the family

indicators.note: one word going about another surrounds it

parts.note: to page someone is to call for them
a plus rent, a regular payment

explanation.surface: A court serves a writ over money owed by a household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue a summons' sounds legal; it only means call someone over a public address.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentage means one's descent or lineage, the line of ancestors that makes up one's family origin.

clue.text: Heard days before, it may instil one with curiosity

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: eves are the days before festivals, as in Christmas Eve
a dropper is the tool for instilling liquid drop by drop

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a medicine bottle that filled a patient with inquisitiveness some days ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Instil is a medical word for putting drops in the eye, which a dropper does.
explanation.definitionFit: An eavesdropper secretly listens to private talk, driven by nosiness or curiosity.

clue.text: American who wrote about Nazis and the force of law?

indicators.note: one word wrapped about another encloses it

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A US author produced books about the Nazis and on law enforcement.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law, as in Westerns.

clue.text: French product marked up in their bistros

indicators.note: in a down clue, written upwards means read from bottom to top
something in the following words lies inside them, spanning the gap

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A French item has its price raised in the cafés of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marked up' reads as a price rise, but it means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese named after the region where it is made.

clue.text: Sounds as if you need the eight-inch

indicators.note: sounding like a word means the answer is pronounced that way

parts.note: this word for a river island is pronounced like the number eight

explanation.surface: A woodworker says the job calls for the eight-inch tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes eight-inch look like a size. An inch is a Scottish word for a small island, and an eyot is a small island in a river such as the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a small island: inch in Scottish place names, eyot or ait on English rivers.

clue.text: Irishman trains soldiers to infiltrate

indicators.note: infiltrating something means getting inside it

parts.note: RY abbreviates railway
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An Irish instructor coaches troops in covert penetration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like a verb; it is the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Rory is a common Irish given name, from the Gaelic Ruaidhrí, so any Rory may be an Irish man.

clue.text: Spinner's terribly rusty — empty victory follows in confusion

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy
letters of rusty rearranged

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: only the outer letters of victory remain

explanation.surface: A bowler is badly out of practice, and a hollow win leaves everyone bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner in cricket is a slow bowler, which is the false trail here; the spinner is a child's top.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsy-turvy means upside down or in utter disorder, so things are in a state of muddle.

clue.text: Trick's rounded off with a musical finale

parts.note: cod as a verb is British slang for to hoax or trick
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick ends with a flourish of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece or movement, its closing section.

clue.text: Something you can't take off until you have put on

definitions.text: Something you can't take off until you have put on

parts.words: Something you can't take off until you have put on
parts.note: surface reading: a riddle about clothing, which must be worn before it can be removed
setter's reading: an aircraft taking off, which passengers may not do until they have buckled up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a truism about clothes; take off is the aircraft leaving the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline passengers must fasten their seat restraint before the plane is allowed to leave the ground.
